title: Milky Way over the VLT
caption: The Milky Way over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The soft glow of the Milky Way stretches across the sky and seems to graze the tops of the enclosures of ESO's Very Large Telescope. The VLT stands at the Paranal Observatory in Chile, a location that ESO says offers some of the most spectacular views of the cosmos.

The band of light is our own galaxy, seen from within. The Sun sits inside a flattened disc of stars, gas and dust. When we look along that disc, the light of a vast number of distant stars blends into a glowing strip, broken up by darker clouds of dust in front of it.

Placing the telescopes against that backdrop connects the instruments with their subject. The VLT's large mirrors are built to gather far more light than any camera lens, so they can study the Milky Way as well as objects far beyond it.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way appears brighter here than it would to someone standing on the platform.
